newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S WOOLWORTHS' WORKERS STRIKE FOR MORE PAY.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S WOOLWORTHS' WORKERS STRIKE FOR MORE PAY.

text.p: About 1,793 employees at South Africa's Woolworths Holdings Ltd, a subsidiary of stores group Wooltru Ltd, have downed tools to push demands for higher pay, Woolworths said on Wednesday.

The company said a meeting was planned for Thursday between representatives of the South African Commercial, Catering and Allied Workers Union (SACCAWU) and employers to try find a solution to a six-day old strike.
"The meeting is currently planned for tomorrow and will be facilitated by the Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration (CCMA)...," Woolworths said in a statement.
It said the strikers, all members of SACCAWU, were demanding a salary increase of 350 rand against the company's offers of 236 rand and 255 rand if they accepted more flexible working conditions.
Woolworths added that despite the strike, trading continued normally as the balance of its 10,000 staffers were not participating in the action.
The CCMA was set up in November in terms of the new Labour Relations Act to provide quick and fair mediation in labour disputes.
